recent_news: May 2026: Shopify announced layoffs affecting 30 employees in revenue operations as part of restructuring efforts. (Source: https://www.interviewpal.com/layoffs/shopify)

November 2025: Shopify made layoffs, stating the changes were intended to remove organizational layers. These affected managerial roles in merchant success, operations, sales, and account executive teams. (Source: https://whittenlublin.com/blog/shopify-layoffs-another-round-of-job-cuts, https://www.linkedin.com/posts/madison-mclauchlan-9730581b5_shopify-says-recent-layoffs-removed-layers-activity-7399211769602387968-huis)
November 2025: Layoffs were influenced by AI. (Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Sj_nJwAm5Z8)

2022 and 2023: Shopify conducted significant workforce reductions due to misjudging the duration of the pandemic-driven e-commerce boom. (Source: https://whittenlublin.com/blog/shopify-layoffs-another-round-of-job-cuts)

July 2022: Shopify planned to lay off 10% of its workers across all divisions, with most cuts in recruiting, support, and sales. (Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2022/07/26/shopify-sinks-12percent-after-company-plans-to-lay-off-10percent-of-workers.html)

company_research.notes: Shopify is a Canadian multinational e-commerce company with 7,600 employees as of July 2026. It operates in the IT Software & Services and E-commerce industries. The company has undergone several rounds of layoffs in recent years, including in May 2026, November 2025, and significant reductions in 2022 and 2023, often citing restructuring, efficiency improvements, and misjudging market conditions. While Shopify promotes an empowering culture with strong values and a focus on employee well-being, there are also signals of fatigue from restructurings, a harder performance tone, and concerns regarding pullbacks on inclusion and a high-pressure environment.
